newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee easier, Jan/March spread narrows.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee easier, Jan/March spread narrows.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures were broadly lower with spot January coming under renewed selling pressure ahead of the first notice day on Thursday.
Traders said the closely-watched Jan/March spread narrowed sharply to $12 by the close from $36 on Friday on concerns over growing nearby supply availabilities.
The month-long tender period for January begins on January 2 after the New Year holiday.
By the close, January shed $35 at $1,250 a tonne while most-active March was off $11 at $1,238. The remaining months were barely traded.
Volume on the exchange reached 3,835 lots.

New York's arabica coffee market was narrowly mixed by midday on Monday as the market took a breather from recent sharp rally on fund buying. Traders are keeping a close watch on a forthcoming independent assessment of the Brazilian 1997/98 coffee crop by former USDA analyst Leon Yallouz after a range of forecasts by trade houses and local sources resulted in conflicting views.
"Everyone is waiting for that," said one trader, adding there was talk that the report could be released early in the New Year.
